back_translations.1: This agreement governs the use of the MedSure Glucose Monitoring System (the "Device") and applies to all patients and caregivers who operate it in accordance with these instructions.
back_translations.2: The user is required to calibrate the Device at least once every 90 days using an approved calibration solution. Calibration records should be kept for reference.
back_translations.3: The Device may be operated above 40°C or below 5°C. Operating outside this range may produce inaccurate glucose readings.
back_translations.4: If the Device fails to operate as described, the user should submit a warranty claim through the MedSure support portal. Claims submitted without a proof of purchase will not be processed.
back_translations.5: Warranty claims must be submitted within 60 calendar days of the failure being discovered. Claims submitted after this period will be denied.
back_translations.6: If an optional extended-service invoice is not paid by the due date, a late fee of 15% of the invoice amount will be applied for each month the payment remains outstanding.
back_translations.7: MedSure retains Device usage data for 24 months to support warranty and safety investigations. Data is deleted afterward unless required by law.
back_translations.8: Any safety incident involving the Device must be reported to the Regulatory Authority no later than March 15, 2027. Late reports may result in regulatory penalties.
back_translations.9: Store the Device and test strips between 2°F and 8°F when not in use. Do not freeze.
back_translations.10: Complaints regarding the Device may be filed with the MedSure Ethics Board (MEB) at any time.
back_translations.11: The Device is designed for single-patient use and may be shared among multiple patients as long as proper cleaning or disinfection is performed.
back_translations.12: The Device measures glucose levels in venous whole blood obtained from a laboratory sample.

11.rationale: Source establishes an absolute, no-exceptions prohibition on multi-patient sharing; back-translation permits sharing conditional on cleaning, a materially weaker safety posture.

12.rationale: Source specifies a capillary fingertip sample; back-translation specifies a venous laboratory sample, a different specimen type the device is not described as validated for.
